Subject: Turnkey deployment coupling — MAP & evaluation cadence

Hi Elena / Tom —

Congrats again on signing. Attached is the first draft of the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that embeds the post-signature implementation plan: rollout tranches, canary windows, migration cutover, and training lanes. Key asks up front:

- Please confirm your preferred canary week (we suggested 2026-07-12 to 07-16 in the doc).
- Procurement: we need a short SOW addendum (billing cadence + acceptance criteria) before we provision dedicated capacity.
- Ops/Eng: review the runbook excerpts in the MAP and flag any infra constraints we should account for.

Attachments: MAP_v1.2_Stageridge.pdf, canary-schedule.csv, runbook-trancheA.odt

High-level plan inside the MAP:
1) Week 0–2: Provision dedicated capacity and coordinate network/VPC peering (pre-signed firewall rules in Appendix B).
2) Week 3: Canary tranche A (2 endpoints, 50 RPS burst-able, shadow mode with 10% traffic split).
3) Week 4–5: Training sprint for platform admins + dev sandbox handoff.
4) Week 6: Migration cutover window (low-traffic overnight) with rollback playbook.

I put Soojin and Laura on copy for the technical and onboarding commitments. Let me know availability for a 45-min alignment call next week (I can do Tue/Wed mornings).

Thanks,
Ben

Elena / team —

Thanks — 15% split is fine but will change the expected token-cost burn rate and may affect autoscaling ramp thresholds in tranche A. Two technical clarifications I added inline in the MAP doc (link below):

- Canary isolation: we recommend running canary endpoints in a dedicated pod pool to avoid KV cache thrash. That is in Section 3.2.
- Latency SLO: we currently measure p95 over 30s windows; to pass your synthetic pass rate we need the synthetic harness to use 8–12 token prompts typical of your workload.

I attached a short runbook excerpt (runbook-trancheA.odt) that lists the rollback gate checks we will execute at +15min, +30min, +90min after canary start. Also attaching a draft canary CSV schedule with exact IP ranges for traffic split.

Two asks for Stageridge ops:
1) Confirm whether your team can create the VPN tunnel or if you need Redwood to initiate (we can take this on but need 5 business days lead).
2) Provide the contact for the on-call person during canary nights (we like an engineering hand to accept rollups).

Link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dQ-Map-Stageridge-eval-plan (I left inline comments)

— Soojin

- Training plan: we'll run a two-day admin workshop (remote) during Week 4 with recordings. Proposed dates: 2026-07-19 and 2026-07-20 (to avoid your PTO week).
- Acceptance gating: propose three measurable gates in the MAP addendum:
  * Synthetic pass rate >= 98% (72h rolling window),
  * p95 latency <= 220ms for baseline prompts,
  * No hotfixes required during final 24h of planned cutover window.
- Canary observers: Redwood will assign an on-call engineer and runbook owner (Soojin). Please confirm your on-call contact by 2026-06-09 so we can add them to PagerDuty escalation.
